headline_marked: Sinner [[ends Djokovic's Wimbledon title bid]], hails him as 'true inspiration'
headline: Sinner ends Djokovic's Wimbledon title bid, hails him as 'true inspiration'
summary: Jannik Sinner delivered a dominant performance, defeating seven-time champion Novak Djokovic in straight sets in the Wimbledon semi-final. He will now face French Open champion Alexander Zverev in Sunday's final.
details: Jannik Sinner secured a commanding victory over defending champion Novak Djokovic in the Wimbledon semi-finals, winning 6-4, 6-4, 6-4. This dominant display on Centre Court ended Djokovic's bid for another title.

Following the match, Sinner praised Djokovic as a "true inspiration," acknowledging the pressure of playing against the world number one. This win avenged Sinner's previous loss to Djokovic at the Australian Open semi-finals in January.
Djokovic, a seven-time Wimbledon champion, once again fell short in his pursuit of a record 25th Grand Slam singles title. This would have broken his tie with Margaret Court.

Despite being 39, Djokovic has shown remarkable longevity, recently winning a five-hour quarter-final against Felix Auger-Aliassime. Sinner noted the high level of play Djokovic continues to produce, calling it an inspiration for younger generations.
Djokovic has dismissed retirement talks, stating his intention to return to Wimbledon at least one more time. Sinner expressed hope that his victory would propel him to a fifth Grand Slam title.
Sinner will now face French Open champion Alexander Zverev in the final on Sunday. Sinner has won his last nine meetings against Zverev, including the 2025 Australian Open final.
However, Zverev has been in superb form, recently winning his first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros. He has shed his "nearly man" tag and poses a significant threat to Sinner's title aspirations.
Sinner acknowledged Zverev's confidence boost from his recent Grand Slam win, stating the final will be "very tough" and different from their previous encounters.
caption:
Jannik Sinner has ended Novak Djokovic's Wimbledon title defense, defeating the seven-time champion in straight sets. Sinner hailed Djokovic as a "true inspiration" after the dominant semi-final victory.

Jannik Sinner secured a commanding victory over defending champion Novak Djokovic in the Wimbledon semi-finals, winning 6-4, 6-4, 6-4. This dominant display on Centre Court ended Djokovic's bid for another title.

Following the match, Sinner praised Djokovic as a "true inspiration," acknowledging the pressure of playing against the world number one. This win avenged Sinner's previous loss to Djokovic at the Australian Open semi-finals in January.

Djokovic, a seven-time Wimbledon champion, once again fell short in his pursuit of a record 25th Grand Slam singles title. This would have broken his tie with Margaret Court.

Despite being 39, Djokovic has shown remarkable longevity, recently winning a five-hour quarter-final against Felix Auger-Aliassime. Sinner noted the high level of play Djokovic continues to produce, calling it an inspiration for younger generations.

Djokovic has dismissed retirement talks, stating his intention to return to Wimbledon at least one more time. Sinner expressed hope that his victory would propel him to a fifth Grand Slam title.

Sinner will now face French Open champion Alexander Zverev in the final on Sunday. Sinner has won his last nine meetings against Zverev, including the 2025 Australian Open final.

However, Zverev has been in superb form, recently winning his first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros. He has shed his "nearly man" tag and poses a significant threat to Sinner's title aspirations.

Sinner acknowledged Zverev's confidence boost from his recent Grand Slam win, stating the final will be "very tough" and different from their previous encounters.

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh-China G2G deal]] opens new horizons for rural development
headline: Bangladesh-China G2G deal opens new horizons for rural development
summary: Bangladesh and China's Fujian province have agreed in principle to forge new government-to-government partnerships across agriculture, rural development, and renewable energy sectors. This collaboration aims to boost agricultural productivity and ensure food s
details: Bangladesh and China's Fujian province have reached an agreement in principle to establish new government-to-government (G2G) partnerships. These collaborations will span key sectors including agriculture, fertilizer supply, rural development, fisheries, food processing, cold storage, and renewable energy.

Detailed discussions on these initiatives took place last Wednesday (July 8) at the Secretariat during a meeting between Bangladesh's Agriculture Minister Amin Ur Rashid Yasin and a Chinese delegation. The talks focused on expanding bilateral cooperation.

Both parties agreed to work jointly on technology transfer, agricultural research, modern farming techniques, improved seeds, food processing, cold chain systems, fisheries development, solar-powered irrigation, and rural infrastructure. The agreement also includes provisions for training, research, and scholarship programs for Bangladeshi agricultural scientists and officials.

A critical agenda point was the urgent renewal of the existing G2G DAP fertilizer supply agreement between Bangladesh and China. The Chinese delegation stressed the importance of renewing the contract before the government's fertilizer procurement begins in the September-October season.

Agriculture Minister Yasin confirmed that the Ministry has already initiated the renewal process, assuring its swift completion to ensure an uninterrupted supply of fertilizer to farmers. Discussions also covered using Fujian's modern agricultural technology to boost rice productivity, process various fruits like jackfruit, develop modern cold chain systems, and establish crab hatcheries.

Further areas of technological cooperation include aquaculture, fish farming, solar-powered irrigation, and the development of coastal saline lands. The Chinese delegation expressed significant interest in providing technology, technical assistance, and potential investment in these sectors.

A high-level Bangladeshi delegation is scheduled to visit Fujian within the next one to two months. The visit will involve meetings with leading research institutions, technology firms, and investors in agriculture, fisheries, food processing, renewable energy, and rural development.

Both sides anticipate that this expanded G2G partnership will significantly enhance Bangladesh's agricultural productivity, strengthen food security, and deepen the long-term development cooperation between Bangladesh and China.
